stories.headline: Tom Brady tops list of athletes who became owners
stories.summary: The legendary quarterback is a member of an exclusive list of athletes that includes LeBron James, Serena Williams and Wayne Gretzky.
stories.body:
Tom Brady is getting (back) into the ownership game.

On Friday, sources confirmed to ESPN and NFL Network that the former superstar quarterback had bought shares in the English soccer giants Chelsea. Brady's purchasing of Chelsea shares comes after he departed the ownership group of another English club, EFL Championship side Birmingham City, earlier in the month after originally becoming a minority owner with a 3.3% stake.

Brady's latest interest isn't his only foray into the world of ownership -- he also owns a 5% minority stake in the Las Vegas Raiders, purchased in 2024, and he also has a stake in the Las Vegas Aces.

The NFL legend is far from the first athlete, active or former, to enter the ownership sphere. Here are other athletes who are now team owners:

Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Atlético Madrid

In October 26 news broke that the star Oklahoma City Thunder guard would be joining the club as an investor.

"I am excited to officially join the group of shareholders of Atlético de Madrid," Gilgeous-Alexander said in the club's post. "This is a club with a long history at the top of European football, and I am grateful for the opportunity to be part of its future."

Jason Kidd -- Everton

In April 2025, English Premier League club Everton announced that then-Dallas Mavericks coach Jason Kidd would be adding a different title to his résumé: ownership group member. The news came after Kidd joined Roundhouse Capital Holdings, which is part of the Friedkin Group -- the U.S. firm that completed its takeover of Everton's ownership the previous December.

Vince Carter, Tracy McGrady, Jozy Altidore -- Buffalo Bills

In December 2024, the Bills announced Carter, McGrady and Altidore were among 10 limited partners the team was adding to its ownership group. Both McGrady (New York Knicks) and Altidore (New York Red Bulls) played for New York-area teams, while Carter spent time with the Brooklyn Nets (who were known as the New Jersey Nets at the time) and was McGrady's teammate on the Toronto Raptors (who are closer to Buffalo than NYC-based teams).

Tom Brady -- Las Vegas Aces, Las Vegas Raiders, Chelsea

The Las Vegas Aces, the reigning WNBA champions, have added to their championship credentials. Seven-time Super Bowl champion Tom Brady acquired a minority stake in the team whose majority owner is Las Vegas Raiders owner Mark Davis.

"I have always been a huge fan of women's sports, and I admire the work that the Aces' players, staff, and the WNBA continue to do to grow the sport and empower future generations of athletes," Brady said in a statement. "To be able to contribute in any way to that mission as a member of the Aces organization is an incredible honor."

Brady attended an Aces game in May 2022 and sent gifts to star Kelsey Plum. Plum and other Aces players were excited to have Brady as part of the team.

He also added the Las Vegas Raiders to his resume after his purchase of minority stake in the franchise was approved by NFL teams owners on Tuesday. The deal was agreed on in May 2023, but it took owners 17 months to give their approval over concerns he was receiving too much of a discount from majority owner Mark Davis.

Brady was also a minority owner of Birmingham City, a club in English soccer's second-tier Championship, but sold his shares in November 2026. He purchased shares in Chelsea later that month.

Lewis Hamilton -- Denver Broncos

The Broncos' ownership group added racing royalty in August 2022. Formula One driver Lewis Hamilton has a stake with the Walton-Penner group, which purchased the team in June 2022.

Hamilton, 37, has the Formula One record for most race wins and has won the Formula One title seven times. The ownership group, which purchased the team for $4.65 billion, is led by Walmart heir Rob Walton and includes former U.S. Secretary of State Condoleezza Rice, who also has a stake.

In April, Hamilton joined with Serena Williams in a consortium led by former Liverpool chairman Martin Broughton in an attempt to buy Premier League club Chelsea.

"He is a champion competitor who knows what it takes to lead a winning team," Walton said in a statement.

Marshawn Lynch -- Seattle Kraken

Lynch spent 13 seasons in Seattle with the Seahawks, but his new sports venture in the state of Washington is on the ice. On April 18, he joined the Seattle Kraken ownership team as a minority investor. The former NFL running back will be a part of the NHL's "Hockey is for Everyone" campaign and Kraken owner Tod Leiweke said Lynch expressed interest in shadowing him to learn hockey CEO operations.

"This is something I never would have imagined," Lynch said to CNBC in a statement. "I always dreamed of playing on a professional team but owning one is something special. As I look back on some of my accomplishments...I'm [going to] continue to count my blessings."

Grammy Award-winning artist and Seattle native Macklemore also joined the Kraken ownership team with Lynch.

Wayne Gretzky, Steve Nash and Dustin Johnson -- Las Vegas Desert Dogs

Wayne Gretzky is a big lacrosse guy? Yep, you read that right. The Great One may have made his name on the ice, but before Gretzky was the pride of the Edmonton Oilers he was a bona fide lax bro.

"The national sport of Canada is box lacrosse," Gretzky said. "I started playing lacrosse on a team at the age of six and played all the way until I was 16 years old. I have a great love for the game in the sense I really think that box lacrosse was such a crucial part of the success I ultimately had in ice hockey."

Because of this, it shouldn't be completely surprising that the hockey legend is linking up with 2020 Masters champion Dustin Johnson, NBA Hall of Famer and current Brooklyn Nets head coach Steve Nash and Nets owner Joe Tsai as part of a star-studded ownership group for the National Lacrosse League's newest expansion team in Las Vegas, the Desert Dogs.

Dwyane Wade -- Utah Jazz

Seeing Dwyane Wade support any team other than the Miami Heat is decidedly jarring. In April, the three-time NBA champion purchased an ownership stake in the Utah Jazz, joining majority owner and team governor Ryan Smith, and expressed a desire to take an active role in the franchise. D. Wade made good on his promise. He could be seen courtside throughout the season; he took action when an unsettling fan incident went down during the postseason, and he became a mentor to then-Jazz star Donovan Mitchell.

The former Miami Heat star also added to his portfolio with something a bit closer to home. Wade, a Chicago native, joined the ownership group of the WNBA's Chicago Sky.

"It's a great opportunity to be a part of the league in its very early stages. ... Growth is going to happen, and so I want to be a part of the growth of this league," Wade said.

Kevin Durant -- Philadelphia Union, NJ/NY Gotham FC

In June 2020, Brooklyn Nets star Kevin Durant purchased a 5% stake in MLS' Philadelphia Union, and he has an option to purchase an additional 5% at a later date. Durant also had engaged in talks about purchasing part of D.C. United the year prior, but he said the discussion never progressed.

Durant expanded his portfolio in May of this year, after being named as a minority owner of the National Women's Soccer League (NWSL) club NJ/NY Gotham FC.

Thirty Five Ventures (35V), a company co-founded by the two-time NBA champion and entrepreneur Rich Kleiman, made a significant investment to acquire a stake in the club, marking the company's second investment in a professional soccer team.

Renee Montgomery -- Atlanta Dream

Former Atlanta Dream guard Renee Montgomery made history in February as part of a three-member investor group that was approved to purchase the team. Montgomery is the first former player to become both an owner and executive of a WNBA franchise. The ownership change followed pressure on former Republican Sen. Kelly Loeffler to sell her share of the Dream, after she angered WNBA players with her opposition to the league's racial justice initiatives.

Patrick Mahomes -- Kansas City Royals

Patrick Mahomes is no stranger to winning. While the Kansas City Royals can't exactly say the same, you can't rule out that the quarterback's winning ways might rub off on the franchise now that he is part of their ownership group. If Mahomes' status as an icon in Kansas City was in question (it wasn't), this move surely cemented it. Becoming a baseball owner made sense on several levels for the Chiefs' QB1. Not only was Mahomes -- who played baseball in college -- a legitimate pro prospect, his father, Pat Mahomes, spent 11 seasons in Major League Baseball. He also had to find some way to put that $503 million contract extension to good use.

Venus and Serena Williams -- Miami Dolphins, Angel City FC

Winning major titles and making history, that's what the Williams sisters do. In 2009, Venus and Serena became the first Black female minority owners in the NFL by purchasing a part of the Miami Dolphins. Musicians Jimmy Buffett, Gloria and Emilio Estefan, Fergie and Marc Anthony also bought shares in the team -- the Dolphins' ownership group is nothing if not eclectic. Then, last year, Serena Williams became part of the star-studded Angel City FC ownership group bringing a NWSL team to Los Angeles in 2022.

Mia Hamm, Abby Wambach and Julie Foudy -- Angel City FC

When Angel City FC arrived on the scene it did so in style. Before we even knew the Los Angeles based NWSL club's name, we knew it had superstar backing like no other. Among the 14 former USWNT players who are part of the group are Mia Hamm, Abby Wambach and Julie Foudy. I would have named Lauren Holiday, Shannon Boxx, Rachel Buehler, Amanda Cromwell, Joy Fawcett, Tisha Venturini Hoch, Angela Hucles, Shannon MacMillan, Saskia Webber and sisters Lorrie Fair Allen and Ronnie Fair Sullins, but I was really trying to stay true to my whole "I'm only going to name 20 athletes" thing from the intro. There are also a bunch of celebrities in the mix, but we don't have that kind of time.

Michael Jordan -- Charlotte Hornets

While we're on the subject of owners who haven't had the type of success we grew accustomed to in their playing days, I would be remiss if I didn't mention the GOAT. In 2010, Michael Jordan became the first ex-player to be a majority owner in the league when the NBA's Board of Governors unanimously approved his $275 million bid to buy the then Charlotte Bobcats in his home state of North Carolina. After a decade of underwhelming years, things look to be on the up for the now Hornets with Rookie of the Year LaMelo Ball providing a long-awaited spark in the organization. Never forget when his dad said he could beat MJ one-on-one ... good times.

Alex Rodriguez -- Minnesota Timberwolves, Minnesota Lynx

I don't know what part of this purchase feels less ideal to me, that Alex Rodriguez and his 50-50 business partner Marc Lore are only pursuing acquiring the Minnesota Timberwolves and Lynx after their original plan to buy the New York Mets failed or that Timberwolves star Anthony Edwards had no idea who former MLB star A-Rod was. Either way, the $1.5 billion deal is expected to close around July 1.

David Beckham -- Inter Miami

David Beckham, iconic soccer player and remains-to-be-seen owner. Beckham -- who is incredibly hands on with the franchise -- is part of an ownership group which was initially called Miami Beckham United but now operates under the name Miami Freedom Park LLC. Beckham and Inter Miami have seemingly been riddled with controversy since the club's inception in 2018. But all those problems could be a thing of the past if Lionel Messi decides to head to MLS. Hey, stranger things have happened.

LeBron James -- Liverpool

Back in 2011, LeBron James and manager Maverick Carter became minority owners of Premier League club Liverpool after Fenway Sports Group, which purchased the team in 2010, became the sole marketer of James' global rights. The deal has turned out to be pretty lucrative for James -- his original stake in the club, valued at about $6.5 million, had grown to about $32 million as of 2018. In 2019, Liverpool won the Premier League for their first top-flight league title in thirty years.

James Harden -- Houston Dynamo, Houston Dash

James Harden might not be in Houston anymore, but the former Rockets superstar's presence is still felt in the city. The Beard purchased a 5% stake in the group that controls MLS' Houston Dynamo and NWSL's Houston Dash in 2019. Boxer Oscar De La Hoya is also part of the group. The Dash won their first NWSL title last year, so he's probably feeling pretty good about that investment.

Russell Wilson and Ken Griffey Jr. -- Seattle Sounders

What do Russell Wilson, Ken Griffey Jr. and Macklemore have in common? They are all part of the Seattle Sounders' ownership group. Wilson, along with his wife, musician Ciara, purchased a stake in the team in 2019 -- just in time for them to win an MLS Cup title. Griffey Jr. and his family followed suit in November 2020.

Zlatan Ibrahimovic -- Hammaraby

Seemingly everything Zlatan does makes people react intensely, and that remained true when he purchased part of Swedish team Hammaraby back in 2019. Fans of Malmo, another Swedish team where Zlatan started his professional career, reacted by vandalizing a statue of Zlatan outside the team's home stadium, placing a toilet seat around one of its arms.

Magic Johnson -- Los Angeles Dodgers

Big LA guy. In 2012, Lakers great Magic Johnson was part of a group that bought the Los Angeles Dodgers from Frank McCourt for a record $2 billion. At the time, the price shattered the mark for a sports franchise. Magic kept it real at the time of purchase when explaining his role in recruiting free agents, saying that while he can't talk hitting or pitching with players, he "can talk winning." If recent history is any indication (in case you blacked out all of 2020 -- the Dodgers won the World Series), it worked.

stories.headline: Kangaroos bounce Kiwis for fourth-straight Rugby League World Cup title
stories.summary: The Kangaroos have won a fourth-straight Rugby League World Cup, toppling New Zealand 32-12 in Brisbane.
stories.body:
The Kangaroos have punished a disappointing New Zealand, with Reece Walsh running riot in a 32-12 World Cup final waltz.

There was an expectation the Kiwis, searching for their second Cup title and first since 2008, would push Australia all the way after a two-point loss in a pulsating tournament opener.

But the visitors struggled from the outset in Brisbane on Sunday night, Jamayne Isaako's kick-off floating long in a sign of things to come.

Walsh dazzled at fullback for the Kangaroos, his pace, vision and wicked footwork too much as he helped lay on two tries and generally wreak havoc around the ruck and close to the line.

Conversely, Walsh's New Zealand opposite Kalyn Ponga -- International Rugby League's Golden Boot winner on Thursday night -- was unable to get into game.

Australian hooker Harry Grant and halves Tom Dearden and Cam Munster completely outplayed their error-riddled opposites, while the Kangaroos' pack muscled up.

Dearden laid on two first-half tries for Liam Martin with well-timed short balls, while Bradman Best was rewarded for an inspired chase-down tackle of Jahrome Hughes with a try soon after.

When Tom Trbojevic scored to begin the second half it was 28-6 and effectively game over.

Jack Bostock completed his breakout season with a try in each half for Australia.

It was the Kangaroos' fourth consecutive title and 10th in the last 11 tournaments, dating back to 1975.

stories.headline: Fantasy baseball: Breaking down Tarik Skubal's fantasy value on the Mets
stories.summary: What Tarik Skubal signing a nine-year deal with the Mets means for his fantasy value.
stories.body:
Two winters ago, the New York Mets opened their wallet to get their offensive centerpiece, Juan Soto. On Sunday, the Mets did the same to get a centerpiece for their rotation, and for a similarly record-setting deal, signing Tarik Skubal to a nine-year, $450 million contract.

Fortunately for us in fantasy, we won't need to spend as much as the Mets did to add Skubal to our rosters, but it's a good landing spot for the lefty. He'll call one of the more pitching-leaning ballparks in Citi Field his home through 2036.

Recent dominance
Skubal's back-to-back Cy Young campaigns of 2024-25 represented the peak of a lengthy stay at the top of the fantasy baseball pitching ranks. In fact, that extended stretch of greatness (spanning games from July 4, 2023, through April 29, 2026) saw him post major league leading totals in wins (41) and WHIP (0.91). He also placed top-five in quality starts (53, 3rd), ERA (2.41, second among those with at least 50 starts) and strikeout rate (31.2%, fifth). Skubal's 1,463 fantasy points scored during that time span were 258 more than the next-closest pitcher.

No other pitcher has had multiple 550-plus-point fantasy seasons since the COVID-shortened 2020. Skubal's were consecutive (2024-25) and he is the first pitcher to do that in back-to-back years since Gerrit Cole, Jacob deGrom and Justin Verlander all did it in both 2018 and 2019.

And that's not to suggest that Skubal has fallen from said peak. Following his trade to the Los Angeles Dodgers at the deadline last year, Skubal's 161 fantasy points scored were only 16 off the lead among pitchers, and he was top-five in the majors in quality starts (7, tied for third) and strikeouts (70, t-3rd) with highly competitive numbers in terms of ERA (2.61), WHIP (1.05) and K% (28.5%).

But the cause of the endpoint of the aforementioned stretch of dominance -- that being, injuries -- largely remain the only concern surrounding Skubal. He underwent surgery in May to remove loose bodies from his elbow, missing 38 games, and he has had two prior arm operations, a Tommy John surgery in 2017 while in college and flexor tendon surgery that cost him a significant chunk of 2022.

That said, Skubal's return after a mere 43-day stint on the injured list this past summer, after which time he posted a 2.71 ERA, 0.97 WHIP and 31.2% strikeout percentage while not missing a single start when including the postseason, demonstrated his otherwise near-infallible ability. Those rates were well within range of his combined numbers from his Cy Young years (2.39 ERA, 0.92 WHIP, 30.3 K%).

No. 1 starting pitcher and top-five overall

In signing with the Mets -- and for that amount of money -- Skubal will need to first pass his pre-signing physical, a step which presumably would bring any immediate and/or serious concerns about his health to light.

Any inherent risk is well worth taking in Skubal's case, especially considering the already risky nature of every front-line starting pitcher in this era. Cam Schlittler and Jacob Misiorowski are both coming off their first-ever seasons as Cy Young-caliber starters, and both saw more than 40-inning jumps (postseason included) from 2025-26. Cristopher Sanchez's skills dipped slightly after the All-Star break. Yoshinobu Yamamoto's volume tends to be reined in by the Los Angeles Dodgers' fluid pitching rotation plans, while Chris Sale's workload was heavily monitored by the Atlanta Braves, which makes sense considering his 37 years of age.

Skubal remains both my No. 1 full-time fantasy starting pitcher -- Shohei Ohtani's hitting contributions coupled with his positional eligibility technically place him atop the list -- and a clear-cut, top-five overall selection in early ESPN standard league drafts. In rotisserie formats, he's a legitimate first-round pick, dependent upon your overall pitching strategy (many managers will not invest their first selection on a pitcher, though it is an entirely defensible position).

That's highly unlikely to change without some sort of signal to the contrary once the anticipated lockout gets resolved and we get further details and reports out of whatever length spring training we get.

stories.headline: NFL Week 11: Big takeaways, questions and fantasy spin from Sunday's games
stories.summary: Our NFL Nation reporters react to all the action, answering the biggest questions coming out of each Sunday game. Here's what we learned from Week 11.
stories.body:
The Sunday slate for Week 11 of the 2026 NFL season began with several blowouts.

With Josh Johnson at quarterback, the Cardinals couldn't get anything going offensively in a loss to the Chiefs. Miami also struggled on that side of the ball against Buffalo in quarterback Kyle McCord's second start. And the Titans' defense allowed touchdowns on the Cowboys' first six drives, leading to a 21-point defeat.

Elsewhere in the early window, the Panthers came out on top of a shootout against the Ravens. The Eagles pulled off an upset over the Steelers with backup quarterback Joe Milton. The Bears won their fifth straight game, while the Lions won in their first game without edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson (knee injury) this season.

In the late window, the Jets snapped a five-game losing streak by defeating the Chargers. Wide receiver Sterling Shepard scored twice for New York after being activated from the practice squad Saturday.

Our NFL Nation reporters react to all the action, answering lingering questions coming out of each game. Fantasy football analysts Matt Bowen and Tristan Cockcroft also have fantasy takeaways from each matchup.

Let's get to it with the biggest lessons from Sunday.

Jump to:

NYJ-LAC | BAL-CAR

NO-CHI | PIT-PHI | TB-DET

TEN-DAL | MIA-BUF | ARI-KC

Catch up on Thursday's game:

IND-HOU

N.Y. Jets 27, L.A. Chargers 24
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Jets
The Jets snapped a five-game losing streak, but was it worth it? Not according to the pro-tank crowd, who watched the Jets all but ruin any hope of landing the No. 1 overall pick in the 2027 draft. Their chances dropped to 1%, per ESPN Analytics. Draft ramifications aside, this was a much-needed win for the Jets (3-8), who matched their 2025 win total with their best offensive performance of the season. Quarterback Geno Smith was nearly flawless as the Jets scored on their first five possessions, ending their TD drought at 10 quarters. A win against a bad team requires proper perspective, but this is certain: They haven't quit on embattled coach Aaron Glenn.

Key stat to know: Wide receiver Sterling Shepard, 33, has been around a long time (11 seasons), but this was the first time he made two touchdown receptions in one game. He was elevated from the practice squad Saturday because of injuries at the position, and he responded with one of the best games of his 120-game career. -- Rich Cimini

Next game: at Dolphins (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Chargers
How much did QB Justin Herbert miss WR Ladd McConkey? Just a week after the Chargers won their first game of the season, they never led in a three-point loss to the Jets. But the connection between Herbert and McConkey, who returned after missing two games because of a back injury, was a positive one for the Chargers as they rallied in the fourth quarter. An offense that has struggled to find impact on the perimeter, McConkey had his third career game with two-plus receiving touchdowns. He entered Sunday's game with one receiving TD this season across six games.

Key stat to know: Sunday's matchup marks the first time Herbert finished a game with more passing touchdowns (two) than interceptions (zero) since a Week 16 win over the Cowboys in 2025. He went 11 straight starts -- including the playoffs -- with at least as many interceptions as he had passing TDs, per ESPN Research. -- ESPN staff

Next game: vs. Patriots (Sunday, 4:05 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: It's been a frustrating season for Chargers RB Omarion Hampton's fantasy managers, but if you've kept your team in the race despite his NFL team's struggles, don't rule out his potential contributions to your stretch run. Over the past two weeks, he has 27.8 fantasy points -- 42 more rushing yards than expected and 6-of-36 carries going for 10-plus yards. That's production that meets the RB2 tier cut-off. -- Cockcroft

Carolina 35, Baltimore 33
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Panthers
Is the Panthers' offense good enough to help them run away with the NFC South? The division-leading Panthers got into a shootout with the slumping Ravens, who had lost five consecutive games coming into Sunday. Led by QB Bryce Young and RB Chuba Hubbard, the offense scored on six different drives. Hubbard, in particular, continued to show why he's the engine that can make big plays on offense, posting his second consecutive two-touchdown game. He has surpassed 100 all-purpose yards in five of the past seven games.

Most surprising performance: CB Will Lee III made a big impact in his return to the lineup. In the first half, the 2026 fourth-round pick took points off the board when he forced a fumble on RB Justice Hill for a touchback. In the fourth quarter, he hit the ball out of RB Derrick Henry's hands, and LB Tyrel Dodson recovered. He finished with four tackles, a pass breakup and two forced fumbles. -- Mike Kaye

Best quote from the locker room: ​When asked if Young's game-winning drives ever get old, DT Derrick Brown said: "Hell no. The goal is to win [laughs], so I'm not going to apologize to no damn body for f---ing how we win. If it takes until the last second, that's what it is."

Next game: at Buccaneers (Monday, 8:15 p.m. ET)

Ravens
Is this the worst Ravens team in recent memory? It's certainly the sloppiest. In losing its sixth straight game, Baltimore was a mess in all three phases. The Ravens' offense committed three turnovers: a game-sealing interception by QB Jacoby Brissett, a fumble by RB Derrick Henry and a fumble by RB Justice Hill. The defense gave up 30 points for the fourth time in five weeks. And on special teams, punt returner LaJohntay Wester muffed two punts. The Ravens are technically still alive for the postseason, falling 2.5 games back of the AFC's last playoff spot. But there's not much faith remaining.

Key stat to know: Without Lamar Jackson (right thumb), the Ravens found other ways to score, becoming the first team in a decade to record a safety and score a kickoff return touchdown in the same game. The last team to do so was the 2016 Chiefs. In the first half, Baltimore got the safety off Mike Green's sack and got the touchdown off Devontez Walker's third career kickoff return. -- Jamison Hensley

Best quote from the locker room: ​Ravens safety Kyle Hamilton on the frustration level of the team: "I don't know if I have been a part of something like this -- definitely not losing six straight. I really don't know what to say at this point, honestly. I've told you everything I could tell you. I'm sure it's tough to come up with new questions at this point and it's tough to come up with new answers. So we're at where we're at."

Next game: at Texans (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Panthers RB Chuba Hubbard continued his clear fantasy RB1 campaign with his fifth game of 20-plus carries and fourth of 24-plus fantasy points in his past seven games. Unfortunately, he has his two most challenging matchups up next: vs. the Buccaneers (Week 12) and Vikings (Week 13). Hubbard's usage props him up as a universal start, but we might be looking at scores in the teens. -- Cockcroft

Chicago 21, New Orleans 13
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Bears
How does Ben Johnson get more of out the offense? Sunday marked Chicago's third win this season despite committing two turnovers, and the offense has yet to figure out how to put teams away early. The Bears need more from their run game after Zavion Thomas' end-around accounted for 30 of their 146 rushing yards. They also need more explosive plays across the board (QB Caleb Williams averaged 6.6 yards per pass). On Thursday, the Bears begin a brutal seven-game stretch vs. four divisional opponents, Jacksonville and Buffalo. To conquer the NFL's hardest remaining schedule, they'll need to get back to looking like the version that beat the Seahawks, Patriots and Falcons.

Most surprising performance: Thomas, a third-round rookie, saw his highest usage on offense all season and recorded a team-high 56 receiving yards on two catches. His speed adds another dimension, which Chicago utilized on the aforementioned reverse, and should earn him more playing time. -- Courtney Cronin

Next game: at Lions (Thursday, 1 p.m. ET)

Saints
Has quarterback Tyler Shough regressed? It has been a tough stretch of games for Shough, who had fewer than 250 passing yards for the second straight game. He also threw an interception for the second straight game and was sacked for a safety. He has been sacked 14 times in the past three games. There are circumstances around Shough's struggles: He was playing with broken bones in his left hand, his starting center and starting right tackle are hurt and the run game has been one of the worst in the league. But the second-year QB has also had a hand in it with some poor decision-making.

Trend to watch: Turnovers, again. CJ Donaldson lost a fumble early in the game, the 11th fumble lost by the Saints this season, which leads the NFL and is only one fumble away from tying last season's total. The Saints were tied for the second-most fumbles in the league last season. -- Katherine Terrell

Next game: at Bengals (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: The Bears' backfield is truly struggling, even with RB Kyle Monangai back in action. D'Andre Swift was held to fewer than 12 fantasy points for a second straight game and fewer than 4.0 yards per carry for a fifth straight; Monangai scored 1.8 points and averaged 2.3 yards per carry. It's difficult to get behind Swift as more than a low-end fantasy RB2, and Monangai is a matchups-oriented flex. -- Cockcroft

Philadelphia 19, Pittsburgh 16
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Eagles
Can the defense lead the Eagles on a mini-run? The defensive line has rounded into form the past two games. They sacked Aaron Rodgers five times after posting five sacks and nine QB hits against the Giants two weeks ago. Edge Jonathan Greenard has been part of that surge with two takedowns in two games after having none before Week 9. It will be a step up in competition on Thanksgiving against Cowboys QB Dak Prescott, but with the Cardinals and Colts up after that, Philly could make things interesting in a down NFC East if the defense continues to shine.

Key stat to know: Saquon Barkley showed a flash of his 2024 form with a 38-yard touchdown run late in the first quarter. It was his 18th career rushing TD of 30-plus yards (including playoffs), passing Jim Brown and Chris Johnson for fourth most in NFL history. The Week 10 bye appeared to be helpful for Barkley, who has been dealing with a hamstring injury. -- Tim McManus

Best quote out of the locker room: When asked about DK Metcalf's history with disqualifications, Eagles cornerback Cooper DeJean said: "I didn't know how many ejections he had or whatever before going into it. But he wasn't getting the ball a whole lot during that game and some receivers could let that get to them. He obviously tried to take it out on me."

Next game: at Cowboys (Thursday, 4:30 p.m. ET)

Steelers
Are the Steelers postseason contenders? The Steelers' record suggests they are, but the eye test says otherwise. With an immobile quarterback and a No. 1 receiver with more penalty yards than receiving yards, the offense is struggling. Aaron Rodgers, who turns 43 in 10 days, has looked every bit his age recently; the Eagles sacked him five times Sunday. Meanwhile, DK Metcalf, who finished with one catch on four targets for 2 yards, was ejected for unsportsmanlike conduct. And with no threat of a passing game, the Eagles shut down the Steelers' run game. The defense eventually settled in, suggesting Pittsburgh might hold their own in the playoffs, but offensive ineptitude might keep it from even getting there.

Key stat to know: Rodgers averaged 0.5 air yards per attempt in the first half -- the lowest air yards per attempt in a half with at least 20 attempts since ESPN began tracking the stat in 2006. Of his 20 first-half attempts, 12 were thrown at or behind the line of scrimmage, and his furthest attempt downfield was for just 8 air yards, per ESPN Research. -- Brooke Pryor

Best quote out of the locker room: Tight end Pat Freiermuth discussed Metcalf's second-half ejection from the game, saying his teammate "knows that's unacceptable. ... He'll be fine." Freiermuth continued: "He's one of my closest [friends] on the team. And so he knows that I have his back in those situations, but it just can't happen."

Next game: vs. Broncos (Friday, 3 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Eagles RB Saquon Barkley scored 13.5 points, rushing for 75 yards and a touchdown on 17 carries. He looked explosive on his 38-yard touchdown run, but he also struggled to find daylight at times. Barkley has a favorable upcoming schedule (@DAL, @AZ, IND), but with limited receiving upside (zero receptions in back-to-back games), he should be viewed as a risk/reward RB2. -- Bowen

Detroit 31, Tampa Bay 21
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Lions
Can the Lions' defense keep delivering without an injured Aidan Hutchinson? The Bucs' offense is not a strong group, so this wasn't the best test. But it was hard to know what to expect from the Lions after they lost their best defender to a season-ending knee injury. Detroit limited Tampa Bay's potent rushing attack and sacked quarterback Baker Mayfield four times. Thanksgiving, however, presents a much tougher test, as the Lions prepare to face the Bears. Chicago has scored at least 20 points in all but two games this season.

What to make of the QB performance: Jared Goff was stellar against the NFL's fourth-ranked defense by ESPN's FPI metric. He threw for 279 yards and two touchdowns while showing more mobility than we usually see from him. Goff eluded rushers and took only one sack despite the Bucs' complex blitz scheme. -- ESPN staff

Next game: vs. Bears (Thursday, 1 p.m. ET)

Buccaneers
With Sunday's loss, how important is next week's game against the Panthers? After winning two in a row, Tampa has now dropped two straight and sits at 3-7. The Bucs blew out the Panthers in Week 7, so a sweep would do wonders for a team whose season is slipping away. On Sunday, the Bucs didn't turn the ball over, but some untimely penalties (RB Bucky Irving had an 80-yard touchdown called back because of a holding penalty) and sacks proved costly. At least there was a bright spot in rookie third-rounder Ted Hurst III, who caught two touchdown passes.

Key stat to know: Irving rushed for a touchdown for a fourth straight game, which marks the longest streak by a Buccaneers player since Earnest Graham had six straight in 2007, per ESPN Research. Irving had two more touchdowns before the streak this season. -- ESPN staff

Next game: vs. Panthers (Monday, 8:15 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: After scoring a career-best 22.6 points, Buccaneers rookie WR Ted Hurst III should be viewed as a potential roster add. He caught 5 of 7 targets, finishing with 56 yards and two touchdowns. Plus, Hurst has the physical traits and speed to win boundary matchups. -- Bowen

Dallas 51, Tennessee 30
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Cowboys
What does beating the one-win Titans mean for the Cowboys' playoff hopes? The Cowboys did what they had to do by beating the Titans. You can scoff at that, but this is a team that lost at home to a then-winless Tampa Bay and a then-two-win Arizona team. The Cowboys' offense was unstoppable -- six touchdowns in their first six possessions -- albeit against a bad defense. Speaking of bad defenses, the Cowboys were incrementally better with Mike Pettine replacing Christian Parker as the playcaller, but they allowed two third-quarter touchdowns, including a 59-yarder when two defenders failed to touch WR Carnell Tate down on the ground. This has to be the formula if the Cowboys want to make it interesting in December.

Key stat to know: CeeDee Lamb is closing in on another No. 88. Lamb surpassed 1,000 receiving yards Sunday, giving him six straight seasons with 1,000 yards. Only Hall of Famer Michael Irvin, another No. 88, has more in Cowboys history with seven. Lamb also had the 50th touchdown catch of his career, tying him for sixth most in team history. -- Todd Archer

Next game: vs. Eagles (Thursday, 4:30 p.m. ET)

Titans
Is this the worst Titans defense ever? The Titans allowed touchdowns on the first six drives by Dallas. The pass rush was virtually nonexistent, and the secondary was unable to cover anyone. The Cowboys rolled to 51 points, making Tennessee the third team since the 1970 NFL merger to allow 40 or more points in four consecutive weeks. This is the second Titans unit to do so, joining the 2004 Titans, who allowed 439 points. This season's Titans have given up 290 points and are on pace for 493. That would be a record for most points allowed by any Titans defense in a season, surpassing the 478 allowed last season.

Key stat to know: The Titans' defense allowed points on 13 straight drives. Per Elias Sports Bureau, that's the longest such streak by any team in a single season since 1978, when full play-by-play data became available. The previous longest streak was 11 straight drives allowed by the Chargers in October 2000. -- Turron Davenport

Next game: at Jaguars (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Titans QB Cam Ward scored 22.22 points, throwing for 248 yards and two scores -- he also had a rushing touchdown. With 19 or more points in three straight games, and his upside as a runner (39 or more rushing yards in two of his past three games), Ward can be played as a QB2/superflex option. -- Bowen

Buffalo 26, Miami 9
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Bills
Will the Bills keep passing like this? Buffalo attempted more passes in the first three quarters on Sunday than it had in any game since Week 1 of 2025. With a crucial stretch of potential playoff previews ahead, starting on Thanksgiving against Kansas City, the Bills just displayed their willingness to let Josh Allen throw the ball 45 times. How much of this is schematic evolution versus gamesmanship (in giving the Chiefs something to think about) is the real question.

Most surprising performance: Coach Joe Brady's decision-making. The Bills rolled the dice with a fake punt early in the first quarter while backed up in their own territory, and then inexplicably lined up for an onside kick up 14 in the fourth quarter. That's not to mention the aforementioned pass-first tactics. -- Nick Suss

Best quote from the locker room: "You guys know, sometimes I wish he wasn't as tough," said Brady on D.J. Moore's value to the Bills. "It pains me to say that. But he's kind of like Josh: When he gets tackled I just hope he gets up because of how important he is. He's as tough as they come."

Next game: vs. Chiefs (Sunday, 4:25 p.m. ET)

Dolphins
Are the Dolphins a better team than their record suggests? On one side of the ball, yes. The defense isn't setting the league on fire, but since their Week 6 bye, they rank top-15 in sacks and top-five in takeaways (grabbing two Sunday). They held two of the top scoring offenses -- the Lions and Bills -- to under their season averages. However, Miami's offense averages the fewest points per game in the NFL and is the driving factor in the team's 1-9 record -- especially without QB Malik Willis. The Dolphins are destined for a top-five draft pick, but their defense has done enough to warrant optimism.

Trend to watch: After intercepting Allen twice, the Dolphins have now taken the ball away in six straight games. Taking it a step further, their rookie class has forced a turnover in all six games, and they're responsible for nine of the team's 11 takeaways this season. -- Marcel Louis-Jacques

Next game: vs. Jets (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Bills WR DJ Moore might have had his share of injuries this season, but he's quite a good fit as QB Josh Allen's No. 1 receiver when healthy. Moore's 23.1 fantasy points and 10 targets were both season bests, and he has at least 16 points in three of his past four games. He's a fantasy WR2 for a competitive stretch of upcoming games (KC, @NE, @GB, CHI, @DEN). -- Cockcroft

Kansas City 34, Arizona 7
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Chiefs
Are the Chiefs ready for the most difficult stretch of the season? After Sunday, the Chiefs appear to be ready. The team is optimistic running back Kenneth Walker III (groin), right tackle Jaylon Moore (right ankle) and right guard Trey Smith (concussion protocol) will all be in the lineup for the Thanksgiving showdown against the Bills. That game starts the lone stretch this season in which the Chiefs will play consecutive road games -- against the Bills, Rams and Bengals. Those three games will likely determine if the Chiefs win the AFC West, and if they stay in the race for the AFC's top playoff seed.

Key stat to know: With two receiving touchdowns, tight end Travis Kelce passed Jimmy Graham for the fourth-most touchdowns (90) by a tight end in NFL history. Kelce also passed Rob Gronkowski for third place for the most total touchdowns (110) -- regular season and playoffs -- by a tight end in league history. -- Nate Taylor

Next game: at Bills (Sunday, 4:25 p.m. ET)

Cardinals
Is it time for the Cardinals to start focusing on next season? As long as rookie Carson Beck is out, yes. The Cardinals' offense is a shell of former itself, and that has nothing to do with Josh Johnson at quarterback. They are starting an easier stretch to end the season that could give them a better chance to evaluate whoever is left to evaluate, which isn't a long list after all the injuries they have suffered. However, if Beck can return at some point this season, then the next six games will give Arizona plenty of time to get a long look at him and decide whether he's their quarterback in 2027.

Key stat to know: Arizona's second-quarter touchdown was its first in 21 drives, which covered two full games -- the loss to the Seahawks, in which they scored just three points, and the Rams loss last week, in which they scored just six points. All nine points were scored on field goals. -- Josh Weinfuss

Next game: vs. Commanders (Sunday, 4:25 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Chiefs TE Travis Kelce scored more fantasy points in this game's first half than he did in any full game since Week 7 of 2023, showing he can still contribute top-shelf production to fantasy managers. He should be a big part of the Chiefs' passing game in upcoming matchups against the Bills (Week 12) and Bengals (Week 14) as well. -- Cockcroft

stories.headline: Reports: Dynamo's Herrera charged with DWI, club aware of 'incident'
stories.summary: Houston Dynamo FC midfielder Héctor Herrera was charged with driving while intoxicated on Saturday in Montgomery County, Texas, according to multiple reports.
stories.body:
Houston Dynamo FC midfielder Héctor Herrera was charged with driving while intoxicated on Saturday in Montgomery County, Texas, according to multiple reports.

MLS and the Houston Dynamo said in a statement to ESPN on Sunday that they are looking into an "incident" involving Herrera.

"The Houston Dynamo are aware of an incident involving Héctor Herrera on Friday night. The Club and Major League Soccer are working to gather additional information," said the Dynamo's statement to ESPN. "We will refrain from providing further comment until appropriate."

The Dynamo are set to begin a best-of-three playoff series against the San Jose Earthquakes on Nov. 24. It is unclear whether Herrera will be available for the match.

The situation could mark another misstep for Herrera, who was sent off in 2024 for spitting on a referee. Following the event, the Dynamo denied his 2025 contract extension, before bringing him back for the 2026 season.

Between 2022 to 2024, Herrera made 69 appearances (including playoffs) for the Dynamo. The Pachuca academy product then made his way to Liga MX's Toluca in 2025, where he won the Clausura and Apertura titles in Mexico's top-flight.

Since his return to Houston in 2026, Herrera has made 30 appearances across the regular season. The midfielder has three goals and two assists this year.

Spotrac's Caleb Pongratz was the first to report the news and the Houston Chronicle published a story Sunday with confirmation of the charge from the Montgomery County sheriff's office.

stories.headline: Alexander-Walker has 27 points as Hawks roll to 107-97 win over Pistons in off game for Cunningham
stories.summary: — Nickeil Alexander-Walker scored 27 points, Atlanta opened the fourth quarter with an 18-0 run, and the Hawks beat the Detroit Pistons 107-97 on Sunday as Cade Cunningham was held to a season-low five points.
stories.body:
ATLANTA -- — Nickeil Alexander-Walker scored 27 points, Atlanta opened the fourth quarter with an 18-0 run, and the Hawks beat the Detroit Pistons 107-97 on Sunday as Cade Cunningham was held to a season-low five points.


Cunningham set a season high with 15 assists but a combination of early foul trouble and a sore knee combined to hold him to 20 points below his average of 25.6 as he made 2 of 9 shots. It was his first game of the season not scoring in double figures.


Corey Kispert scored a season-high 18 points and Lu Dort had 16 in the Hawks' fourth straight win.


Isaiah Joe led Detroit with 19 points. Ausar Thompson and John Collins had 18 and Paul Reed added 16.


The Pistons led 85-74 at the start of the fourth quarter before the Hawks took a 92-85 with the 18 unanswered points. Joe's 3-pointer with 4:52 remaining ended Detroit's scoreless streak.


Cunningham picked up two fouls in the first period and was called for his third foul early in the second. He was limited to 14 minutes in the first half while missing all three of his shots from the field.


Cunningham scored his first points with a jumper off the glass early in the second half but continued to focus on setting up shots for teammates while receiving extra defensive attention from Dyson Daniels and the Hawks.


Cunningham was included on Detroit's injury report with right knee soreness. Coach J.B. Bickerstaff said before the game protecting Cunningham was “the most important thing. He’s a competitor and wants to play. But it’s also our responsibility to just make sure that we’re protecting him at all costs.”


Cunningham was held out of Detroit's 122-109 win at New Orleans on Wednesday night but scored 23 points in a 105-102 loss to Toronto on Friday night.


Hawks rookie Kingston Flemings had 10 points after missing three games with a sore back.


Up next
Pistons: Play at Orlando on Tuesday night.


Hawks: Visit Boston on Friday night.

stories.headline: Bruno Fernandes disputes Leny Yoro red card in Liverpool's rout of Man United
stories.summary: Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes was not happy with the officiating in Sunday's 4-0 drubbing at Liverpool.
stories.body:
Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes was not happy with the officiating in Sunday's 4-0 drubbing at Liverpool, insisting Leny Yoro's early challenge on Alexander Isak was "never a red card."

Yoro was dismissed in the eighth minute by referee Sam Barrott for what was deemed a last-man foul that denied Isak a goalscoring opportunity following Matthijs de Ligt's mistake, with Dominik Szoboszlai scoring from the resulting free-kick.

The Reds went on to complete a comprehensive rout over the 10 men with further goals from Florian Wirtz, Rio Ngumoha and Víctor Muñoz as Mauricio Pochettino's Red Devils reign got off to a miserable start at Anfield.

The new head coach said he took full ownership of the result but felt the Yoro sending off changed the course of the game, with his skipper in agreement and feeling the wrong decision had been reached.

The Portugal midfielder told BBC Sport: "I can understand the fall, but it's never a red card.

"I think it's too many referees on the pitch and too many on VAR, seated, with such a long time to see and put it back, go forward, put it back, do it in slow motion, whatsoever.

"To make a mistake like this can change a game. But obviously, then, it's not because of them that we concede the goal from the free-kick, but it changes completely the flow of the game."

stories.headline: AFL Draft 2026: Grading the draft hauls for every club
stories.summary: The 2026 AFL Draft has been run, but which team won? ESPN's draft expert Jasper Chellappah has handed down five As and two Ds after this year's two-night affair.
stories.body:
The 2026 AFL Draft has been run and done, so let's get into grading each team's haul. Night one was headlined by a Brisbane points matching debacle, with the Swans landing Caylen Murray.

It flipped the script for teams down the order with the Saints and Pies landing their preferred prospects thanks to Brisbane's three-point miss on Murray.

On night two there was a clear directive from clubs to draft based on list need. With the crop of talent 15 past 40 so even this year, clubs were focused on specific roles that suit the modern game and it resulted in bolting mature-agers earning main list opportunities.

These draft grades aren't just based on the calibre of talent brought into the club - it was a lot easier for Port Adelaide and Carlton to land star youngsters than North Melbourne and Geelong. It takes into account live trading, value on each pick and positional fits at the club.

These are ESPN's draft grades for every club after the 2026 AFL Draft.

READ: 'No one saw it coming' - Inside the Swans' draft heist that landed a Lions Academy star

Adelaide
Pre-draft hand: 15, 32, 35, 43, 54

Selections: Toby Krasna (14), Xavier Ladbrook (34), Sam Tassone (44)
There was a clear plan from the Crows to address their transition ball movement, and they've done so here. Krasna is an outside midfielder that really came on this year with his class in space. He runs hard both ways, plays with flair on the ball and is incisive with his foot skills in the forward half.

Xavier Ladbrook will take time to develop as a 202cm key defender that needs time in the gym, but his running base and length gives him an exciting platform. It was rounded out with local dasher Sam Tassone who has some raw, developable traits with speed out of defence.

The Crows passed up Anthony Long after Geelong's bid on the NGA forward.

Grade: B-

Brisbane
Pre-draft hand: 21, 27, 28, 45

Selections: Kodah Edwards (27), Archie Van Dyk (28), Jackson Phillips (29), Archie Spencer (36)

We haven't seen a bid matching debacle quite like Brisbane's on night one when they fell three points short of keeping Caylen Murray. The Lions cornered themselves and found no trade partner on the clock.

It meant they unexpectedly carried three selections back to back early on night two, opting for two South Adelaide products in Edwards and Van Dyke as they addressed their midfield mix.

Edwards captained SA and has versatility to play on-ball or through the forward 50, while Van Dyk has the size and skill to develop rapidly in a professional environment.

Phillips looks a natural wingman at the next level with good ball use off both feet and disciplined running patterns. He looks most likely to play senior football early next year, and they rounded out with dashing defender Archie Spencer.

Grade: D

Carlton
Pre-draft hand: 13, 18, 31, 50, 59, 67, 73

Selections: Cody Walker (3), Harvey Spawton-Guy (32), Jackson Watkins (37), Ethan Herbert (46)

A nice mix of prospects for the Blues began with the arrival of Cody Walker early on night one. The gifted midfielder has Brownlow upside in his prime as a natural ball-winner that puts speed on the game with aggressive movement.

WA's Harvey Spawton-Guy will be looked at as a tall to develop at both ends of the ground - he competes superbly in the air and that attack on the footy bodes well. Jackson Watkins plays with power in the forward half as a smaller type and Ethan Herbert's upside as a ruck of the future is enticing with his ball-winning and skill around the ground a point of difference.

Grade: A-

Collingwood
Pre-draft hand: 11, 30, 63, 64, 65

Selections: Sam Gayfer (12), Gus Kennedy (31), Jordan Knapp (41), Koby LeCras (62)

This is some sort of result for the Pies. They had Gayfer circled on their board from a long way out and were delighted to find him available. His courage and strength in the air at a combine-record vertical leap will be a nightmare to defend.

Kennedy is one of the great characters of the class and plays with a lot of energy off halfback, while Knapp is an exceptional ball magnet through the midfield but will need to build size at the next level.

Rounding out a significant haul was one of the big sliders Koby LeCras. The nephew of premiership Eagle Mark, the 192cm forward can roam up wings with a big engine and is a beautiful kick around goals off his preferred left.

Grade: A

Essendon
Pre-draft hand: 1, 17, 25, 69, 75, 78, 80 (plus second round compensation pick)

Selections: Ethan Drever (2), Archie Elliott (17), Harvie Cooke (21), Jack Pickett (26), Blake Justice (55)

The Bombers had a lot of work to do on each night and they will come away happy with the draft haul. Drever is the perfect complement to previous drafts through the midfield as the outside speed and damage, rating him as the No. 1 player in the open pool.

They paired him with best mate Archie Elliott which produced the best moment of night one as he was pulled out of the crowd at Marvel Stadium. The small forward is an excellent aerialist and has a defensive edge to his game that appeals.

Harvie Cooke was the Talent League's best and fairest and will suit a high half forward role at the next level, while the 194cm Jack Pickett is the big upside swing in the second round as the most accurate set shot to come through the pathways in some time. He will take time as he rehabs a torn ACL and MCL.

The Dons rounded it out with NGA Blake Justice who will be a slow starter to pre-season with a hamstring, but the 192cm midfielder has a unique blend of speed, agility and height that is exciting to develop.

Grade: B+

Fremantle
Pre-draft hand: 19, 40, 58, 61, 68

Selections: George Dimer (18), Kane Johnston (42), Jake Medved (57)

The Dockers have some ready-made options to add depth on a flag tilt. They were delighted that Dimer got through a host of suitors late on night one, and he looms as an immediate Switkowski replacement. Dimer is ultra-clean below his knees at 173cm and sets up teammates selflessly.

Kane Johnston is a 24-year-old tall out of the WAFL that's played his best footy in the forward 50 but could be utilised in defence. His body is ready to compete and the athleticism is AFL level.

Fremantle pinched Jake Medved out of the Swans Academy to round out their night. The utility has played in just about every position this season but could be best used as a wingman with his ranginess and endurance base.

Grade: C+

Geelong
Pre-draft hand: 36, 55, 60

Selections: Lachie Hicks (38), Anthony Long (56), Zach Stevens (60)

This was a quintessential Cats draft. They entered late on night two and immediately took a swing on one of the best athletes in the draft. Hicks has the speed-endurance blend Geelong covets, covering big distances and racking up the ball all season for the Western Jets.

Anthony Long was one of five(!) academy prospects they bid on late. The Crows NGA prospect is Izak Rankine's cousin and brings sharp agility and forward 50 creativity at 184cm.

Finally, Zach Stevens was the classic local product pick out of South Barwon. He's possibly the fastest product to be drafted and as a half forward showed flashes in the VFL and at Talent League levels.

Grade: B

Gold Coast
Pre-draft hand: 8, 70, 72, 77

Selections: Leo Steed (10), Elliott Himmelberg (63), Jamarra Ugle-Hagan (64)

The Suns took one live pick to the draft via Ben King's compensation. They opted for the midfield option in WA's Leo Steed, whose clean hands, strong transition running and fantastic work ethic rocketed his stocks this year. Steed has balance and selflessness to his game.

They rounded out the draft with two rookie elevations.

Grade: C

GWS
Pre-draft hand: 9, 20, 26, 57

Selections: Ethan Matthews (6), Jake Eime (13), Andrio Sousa (45)

Matthews is the best academy prospect GWS has had since Tom Green, and the earliest they've ever taken in a draft. The Giants moved up as far as they could so their residual draft pick would sit in the teens and with that pick they opted for Jake Eime.

A very Giants-esque selection, the SA product is an aggressive rebounder off halfback with the dare to tuck the ball and take on opponents. He can finish off transition in the forward half with good disposal and forms an exciting combination with Lachie Ash.

On night two Andrio Sousa presented as a fantastic athlete to develop on a wing or forward flank, though in isolation trading pick 20 to the Power for a future second-rounder was a poor return.

Grade: B-

Hawthorn
Pre-draft hand: 29, 37, 66, 74

Selections: Benji Van Rooyen (30), Cooper Hodge (58), Keenan Boi (59)

The Hawks targeted a real list need with Van Rooyen, the younger brother of Melbourne's Jacob. He's a legitimate ruck size and uses his physicality in the air well, enjoying the best championships of any ruck this year playing for WA.

The Cats made sneaky bids on Luke's son Cooper Hodge and Keenan Boi, with the latter sliding through to make for a comfortable bid match. Hodge's best traits come in the contest where he's tough and aggressive, while Boi has a lot of power in the forward half.

Grade: C+

Melbourne
Pre-draft hand: 4, 14, 48, 51, 79

Selections: Mitch Harris (7), Lochie Burrows (15), Ben Forster (49), Kaie Sullivan (52)

The Dees had another two first-rounders to play with and opted for the top key defender in Harris. His form a SANFL League level to finish the season cemented his top-10 status and Melbourne will look to him and Disco Turner as the future combination in defence.

Lochie Burrows is one of the best characters in the draft and gives the Dees huge flexibility as a halfback or hard-nosed on-baller. Ben Forster is a role player swing late in the draft with the wingman running hard both ways and offering neat skills in space. Kaie Sullivan was the late-season boater out of the Stingrays after a huge finals campaign elevated his stock off half forward.

Grade: B

North Melbourne
Pre-draft hand: 33, 49, 62

Selections: George Gale (23), Seb Marsic (35), Aidan McCartney (54)

The Roos traded their future first-rounder to get in for George Gale, such was their plaudits of the hardened youngster. He runs hard as an outside midfielder and has the size to eventually transition inside, but looks like a disciplined role player that will allow others to shine early in his career.

Seb Marsic was a bolter on night two as a big, physical key forward. He kicked seven goals in a game that North's Ollie Griffin kicked four at the other end.

The Aidan McCartney bid was matched late on night two with the 195cm son of Jason finding his way to Arden St.

Grade: B-

Port Adelaide
Pre-draft hand: 7, 12, 22, 24, 34, 46

Selections: Dougie Cochrane (1), Clancy Snell (19), Wil Malady (20), Wil Antrobus (25), Gabriel Patterson (39), Angus White (47)

The draft of the year goes to Port Adelaide. Dougie Cochrane was only the start for them, but it was a big one with the consensus best prospect in the pool becoming Port's first-ever No. 1 pick.

Shrewd live trading landed picks 19 and 20 and they grabbed sliders. Clancy Snell is one of the best interceptors in the crop and at 197cm will play on a range of forwards. Wil Malady is an upside swing on the clear talent. The 190cm forward is athletic and brilliant in the air.

Wil Antrobus was an early call at pick 25 but fits a clear need out of defence. His left leg is lethal in open play and he can be relied upon to kick in. They finished off with local products - Gabe Patterson plays with power in the forward half while Angus White has rehabbed an ACL this year but adds speed through the midfield.

Grade: A+

Richmond
Pre-draft hand: 2, 5, 44, 76 (plus second round compensation pick)

Selections: Arki Butler (4), Harry Van Hattum (8), Noah Williams (22), Harry Franz (51)

Richmond landed open prospects at 1 and 3 in ESPN's Power Rankings. Arki Butler, the match-winning medium forward, and Harry Van Hattum, the standout ruckman, are upside swings into the future. Neither can be expected to hit the ground running fully next year but could spearhead the Tigers into a new era.

Noah Williams was a smart choice at 22 with his competitiveness through the midfield and in defence giving him the versatility to play early. Richmond finished their draft with Harry Franz, a high-flying 194cm defender out of SA that plays with physicality.

Grade: A+

St Kilda
Pre-draft hand: 10, 16, 41

Selections: Gustavo Teixeira (11), Tyson Bradley (16), Lewis Houndsome (43)

The Saints could not believe their luck when Brisbane didn't match on Caylen Murray and Gus Teixeira slid all the way through to 11. A genuine first overall pick chance at stages this year, Teixeira has power, class and upside in the forward half.

They nabbed another bayside product at 16 in Vic Metro MVP Tyson Bradley. At 195cm he should grow into the physical key defender that takes on the big forwards at AFL level.

St Kilda finished off night two with Lewis Houndsome, a big key forward that's played well through the ruck but struggled with injuries after a promising bottom-age campaign.

Grade: A

Sydney
Pre-draft hand: 6, 38, 39, 47

Selections: Caylen Murray (9), Brady Wright (40), Mitch Knevitt (48), Mason McGroder (61)

It was a bold and brilliant coup to land Murray, but it remains to be seen if he was best available for the Swans at that point. It's a clear list need with the departure of Nick Blakey in the off-season; Murray offers dash and class off halfback, being one of the most reliable distributors in the crop and offering midfield upside.

Brady Wright was prolific for Werribee in the VFL, and the 194cm goalkicker is a best 23 candidate next year after winning the Fothergill-Round-Mitchell Medal. They added to their mature-age pickups with delisted Cat Mitch Knevitt, whose size around the ball could prove valuable.

Mason McGroder didn't attract a bid until pick 61 which made matching a formality. The long jumper won silver at the U20s World Games in Oregon this year and presents as one of the best athletes to ever come into the AFL system.

Grade: B+

West Coast
Pre-draft hand: 3, 23, 56 (plus second round compensation pick)

Selections: Heath Mellody (5), Jake Soutar (24), Harper Banfield (65)

The pickups are solid for the Eagles, but the way they approached this draft is up for debate for a second straight year. Despite being armed with more list spots than any team in the competition thanks to assistance packages, they were once again caught out this week, not turning over enough primary list spots.

West Coast traded a valuable second-rounder into next year, receiving North's future first in the heavily-compromised 2027 draft -- Tasmania's first. As a result they only took the three picks this time around -- a disappointment for a rebuilding side -- all from WA.

Heath Mellody is the best WA prospect since Luke Jackson, providing the outside run and carry that clubs covet. He's an elite kick and fits alongside Harley Reid and Willem Duursma superbly. Jake Soutar is the readymade option and they went early on the 20-year-old. He's a natural interceptor at 190cm and will likely play on third talls next year.

They rounded out the night by taking father-son Harper Banfield with their natural selection after a bid didn't materialise. He's a strong-bodied midfielder with an elite endurance base.

Grade: D+

Western Bulldogs
Pre-draft hand: 42, 52, 53, 71

Selections: Khaled El Souki (33), Jack Riding (50), Sam Devers (53)

It was an uncomfortable wait through night one and early parts of night two for a bid on El Souki to arrive. The small forward NGA landed in an ideal part of the draft for the Dogs to match and the eruption from El Souki's family and friends was worth the wait. His physicality, left foot and goal sense gives him an elite platform to blossom at the Dogs.

The 26-year-old Jack Riding has toiled away with Werribee to earn this opportunity, and is drafted with a role for him in the forward 50. He's a beautiful crumber of the ball and has mixed it in senior football already.

Sam Devers is an upside play as a 189cm defender that straight lines the ball and puts speed on the game. He took time returning this year after a shoulder reconstruction.

Grade: B

stories.headline: Max Verstappen, George Russell's latest war of words unlikely to stay in Vegas
stories.summary: The long-standing Max Verstappen-George Russell feud boiled over in Las Vegas, where the victorious Dutchman took delight in his rival's misfortune.
stories.body:
Max Verstappen took immense pleasure in watching George Russell's Mercedes disappear from his rearview mirrors and go nose first into the barriers on the penultimate lap of Formula 1's Las Vegas Grand Prix. The four-time world champion made no effort to disguise his glee over team radio in the immediate aftermath and then, once he had gone on to win Saturday evening's race, doubled down in his derision of the Mercedes driver while speaking to the media.

"It was honestly fantastic when I looked in my mirror and I saw what was happening," Verstappen said in a postrace news conference. "I was like, 'Fantastic, my day is only getting better.' And of course, when I then crossed the line in first, my day was complete."

The comments will likely fuel an already-heated rivalry between the two drivers -- not least because Verstappen didn't stop there. Speaking to Dutch broadcaster Viaplay soon after, he also took aim at Russell's ability behind the wheel and disappointing season, saying the 28-year-old Briton was "all talk off the track and a complete joke on it."

By the time Verstappen's comments were lighting up social media like a jackpot-winning slot machine, Russell had already finished his media duties in Las Vegas, meaning he will likely wait until the paddock reconvenes in Qatar next week to give his response. But based on the pair's history, it seems incredibly unlikely he will take the criticism lying down.

In a sport in which many of the competitors are now remarkably friendly -- to the point that six drivers holidayed together between this year's races in Azerbaijan and Malaysia -- the animosity between Russell and Verstappen is real. But how did the relationship between the two drivers, who have never been teammates nor fought head-to-head for a title, sour to this level?

'Princess George' and 'borderline violence'
The first sign of public animosity between the two drivers emerged following the sprint race at the 2023 Azerbaijan Grand Prix. Russell and Verstappen collided while fighting for position in the opening corners of the race, with the contact punching a hole in the side of Verstappen's Red Bull.

Staring at the damage in disbelief after the race, Verstappen, who went on to finish ahead of Russell, confronted the Mercedes driver as he walked past him in parc fermé. When Russell brushed aside Verstappen's complaints, saying "I didn't have any grip," the 29-year-old Dutchman appeared genuinely insulted and retorted, "We all had no grip!" Russell then dismissively walked away from the argument, with Verstappen calling after him, "Expect next time the same, d---head!"

The drama was caught on one of F1's roving cameras in the pit lane, making the exchange the main talking point after the race. Speaking to Dutch journalists in the paddock, Verstappen labeled his rival "Princess George," while the Mercedes driver told TV crews he was genuinely "surprised" by how angry Verstappen had been.

If nothing had followed the Baku collision, the incident could have been written off as a one-off quarrel in the heat of the moment. But over the following years, it became clear there was a serious grudge from both sides.

The next time the spat went public was at the 2024 Qatar Grand Prix, where Verstappen was given a one-place grid penalty for driving slowly on a preparation lap in qualifying. The penalty moved Russell onto pole position, but Verstappen felt his rival -- who had to take evasive action around Verstappen while on a warmup lap of his own -- had gone out of his way to get Verstappen penalized in the stewards' room.

"I find it ridiculous how [he] wants to make sure I get a penalty," Verstappen said at the time. "You know what it is? He acts decent in front of the camera here, but when you talk to him personally, he is a different person ... I can't stand that. In that case, you can better f--- off."

A week later at the final round of the season in Abu Dhabi, Russell responded to Verstappen's comments, claiming the Dutchman threatened him with "borderline violence" after the stewards' briefing.

"I find his comments pretty ironic when he comes out and says, 'I'm going to purposefully crash into you, I'm going to put you on your f---ing head in the wall.' For me, that isn't acceptable and he's gone beyond the line here, and I'm not going to accept it," Russell said. "So somebody's got to stand up to a guy like this before it gets out of control.

"All of this is racing, but he's felt the need to take it personal. I have no idea why he's done that, and he cannot deal with adversity.

"Whenever anything is not going his way, he lashes out with unnecessary anger and borderline violence. We've seen it in Brazil in the past with [Esteban] Ocon, we saw it in '21 with Lewis [Hamilton], in Mexico with Lando [Norris], in Budapest when he didn't have the most dominant car, crashes into Lewis, slamming his whole team. That is not a guy who I respect, and I wish he would be a better role model."

When Russell's quotes were put to Verstappen, it only upped the ante in the paddock's latest war of words.

"I didn't say it like that," Verstappen responded. "But you know, that's another thing. That happened behind closed doors, so you don't have to share everything that was said there and make it more dramatic.

"But you know, those things don't surprise me. I just give my opinion about how he is. Of course, he's not happy with it, but it's the same thing he did at the stewards. Lying and putting things together that aren't correct.

"He's a backstabber. It doesn't matter to me. You don't have to talk too much about people like that, they are just losers."

That same weekend in Abu Dhabi, the full F1 grid met for a dinner as part of an ongoing tradition among drivers to spend at least one evening per year as a complete group. Speaking on the "Pitstop" podcast later the same month, Liam Lawson told a story of how the weekend's bickering in the paddock spilled over to the dinner table.

"This is f---ing funny. It's really funny," Lawson said. "We rock up, at this big table. As the table was filling up, that side of the table was pretty much full, and opposite me was Max and then three chairs to the left [of him]. George hadn't turned up at this point.

"We all said, 'We're going to save the spot for George right next to Max.' George arrives and Max said, 'Mate, we've saved a seat for you.' And George just picks up the chair and walks to the other end of the table and sits with Lewis at that end of the table."

The next flashpoint came at the 2025 Spanish Grand Prix, when Verstappen crashed into the side of Russell's car -- seemingly out of pure frustration. The collision happened shortly after a late safety car period had left Verstappen on worn tires in the fight against his rivals and scuppered his chances of a podium finish.

Russell attempted a move on Verstappen at Turn 1 that resulted in the Mercedes driver sliding into Verstappen, forcing the Red Bull driver off the track. The stewards launched an investigation into the incident, which Red Bull feared might result in Verstappen receiving a penalty for leaving the track and gaining an advantage.

Verstappen's engineer, Gianpiero Lambiase, radioed his driver to tell him to give the position back to Russell to avoid a potential penalty -- much to the frustration of Verstappen. On the approach to Turn 5 on the following lap, Verstappen appeared to cede the position to Russell, only to accelerate again before the apex and collide with the Mercedes.

The stewards deemed Verstappen entirely at fault for the collision and issued a 10-second penalty -- dropping him to 10th place at the finish -- as well as three penalty points on his superlicense, bringing him just a single point from a race ban. Although Verstappen later admitted the incident "should not have happened" in an Instagram post -- as close to an apology as you'll likely get from the Red Bull driver -- Russell still took the opportunity to take a sideways dig at his rival.

"I was a bit surprised to see him taking responsibility, because it's quite unlike him," he said. "We actually bumped into each other at the airport a few days ago, but we didn't even chat about it. He was there with his family and his newborn, chatting about how that was going. He was busy folding the pram and trying to get it through the security scanner.

"Had I been taken out of the race, I'd be feeling very differently for sure. Ultimately, his actions benefitted me, cost him, and I should say thanks."

The pair then lined up on the front row of the grid for the next race in Canada, leading Russell to make a pointed joke about how close Verstappen was to a race ban.

"We're mates so it's all good," Russell said when asked about the potential for a collision at the first corner. "I've got a few more points on my license to play with! So ... let's see."

Verstappen was said to be annoyed by the comments and another row broke out after the race when Red Bull tried to get Russell disqualified for driving erratically behind a safety car. Verstappen had briefly overtaken Russell when the Mercedes driver hit the brakes to warm his tires behind the safety car, and Red Bull protested the move following the race, only for the appeal to be thrown out by the stewards several hours later.

As an aside, but another example of Verstappen's tendency to hold a grudge, the incident with Russell at the Spanish Grand Prix was referenced in the postrace news conference at the season-deciding Abu Dhabi Grand Prix. When a journalist asked Verstappen if he regretted the incident given that he lost the title by fewer points than the penalty cost him in Spain, the Red Bull driver responded, "You forget all the other stuff that happened in my season. The only thing you mention is Barcelona. I knew that would come. You're giving me a stupid grin now."

Nearly four months later, at this year's Japanese Grand Prix, Verstappen refused to start his news conference until the same journalist had left the room.

What happened in Vegas is unlikely to stay in Vegas
Coming back up to speed under the bright lights of Las Vegas on Saturday night, and Russell and Verstappen spent the first half of the race trading position at the front of the field -- invariably with Verstappen coming out on top.

Russell, who desperately needed a victory to salvage something from the most bruising season of his career, appeared to be overdriving each time he got his nose ahead of the Red Bull. If Russell took the lead into Turn 14, Verstappen always had an answer, whether it came through the high-speed Turn 17 on the following straight or by waiting for Russell to go deep at Turn 1 and retaking the position in Turns 2, 3 and 4.

Things got worse for Russell on lap 38 when he slipped behind teammate Kimi Antonelli to third place, meaning as the laps counted down, he needed to do something extra special to move up two positions and salvage victory.

With two laps of the 50-lap race remaining, he resorted to a high-risk, late-braking attempt on Antonelli at Turn 5. Only a few drivers had made such a pass stick all evening, and as Russell found himself off the racing line, a combination of debris and dust resulted in a lock-up and light contact with the barrier in the run-off area.

"Ha ha, well done! My God," Verstappen laughed over team radio as he watched events unfold behind him.

Russell managed to extricate his car from the barrier, but the time lost returning to the track meant he could only manage a ninth-place finish at the checkered flag.

Verstappen's desire to comment so publicly about Russell's misfortune was notable and no doubt at the front of his mind due to an incident between the two drivers during final practice in Las Vegas the day before.

A loose gentleman's agreement exists between drivers to wait in line to start a fast lap in practice, and Verstappen essentially tried jumping the queue ahead of Russell on the back straight toward the end of the session. Russell, aggrieved by the move, then attempted to repass Verstappen ahead of Turn 14 -- the last braking zone before the start of a new lap -- but in doing so was squeezed to the inside of the track by the Red Bull, resulting in a light brush of wheels between the two cars at the apex.

In the eyes of the stewards, the incident only warranted giving a warning to Verstappen for movement under braking, but in the furious microclimate of the Verstappen-Russell rivalry, it added fuel to the fire once more.

Speaking after the qualifying session that followed final practice, Russell built on his previous rhetoric that Verstappen acts like a paddock bully.

"I am not just going to accept somebody to screw me over like this and walk around like they are bigger and better than everyone else," Russell said. "Somebody has got to stand up to that guy."

Immediately after qualifying, Verstappen refused to acknowledge the practice incident but couldn't resist sticking the knife in after his victory on Saturday. In an interview with Dutch broadcaster Viaplay, he was asked if the win had been in some way been inspired by Russell's quotes the previous day.

"His comments don't motivate me, because he's nowhere near me," Verstappen responded. "All talk off the track and a complete joke on it this season. Perfect karma."

The 2026 title battle may be over, but the drama in the F1 paddock never stops. Expect this one to continue at the final two rounds in Qatar and Abu Dhabi.

stories.headline: Champions League upstarts Como suffer Moise Kean injury blow
stories.summary: Como forward Moise Kean is set to be out injured for at least two months and could miss Champions League games against Paris Saint-Germain and Barcelona.
stories.body:
Como forward Moise Kean is set to be out injured for at least two months, his coach Cesc Fabregas said on Friday, and could miss Champions League games against Paris Saint-Germain and Barcelona.

The 26-year-old Italy forward injured his right leg against Belgium in the Nations League this week but the latest issue was with his left leg, Fabregas said.
